blogs.title: Why Angles Matter: The Science Behind Orthogonal Finetuning for Diffusion Models
blogs.description: A lay‑person’s deep‑dive into the core insight of the paper – that the directions (angles) of neurons encode most of the semantic knowledge in a model. The post explains hyperspherical energy, uses intuitive visual analogies (like rotating vectors on a globe), and shows why preserving these angles with orthogonal transformations keeps a diffusion model’s creativity intact while allowing control.

blogs.title: From DreamBooth to OFT: Making Subject‑Driven Image Generation Faster and Safer
blogs.description: Explains how Orthogonal Finetuning (and its constrained variant COFT) improves subject‑driven generation. The blog walks through the classic DreamBooth workflow, its pitfalls (identity loss, training instability), and how OFT’s orthogonal tweaks keep the subject’s identity while converging in fewer steps, backed by easy‑to‑understand graphs and example images.

blogs.title: Controlling Diffusion with No Extra Overhead: Orthogonal Finetuning vs. ControlNet
blogs.description: Compares traditional control methods (ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter, LoRA) with OFT for tasks like edge‑to‑image, segmentation‑to‑image, and landmark‑to‑face. The article breaks down the new "control consistency" metric, highlights OFT’s faster convergence and higher fidelity, and shows why there’s no additional inference cost.

blogs.title: Inside the Math: How Cayley Transforms and Block‑Diagonal Orthogonal Matrices Make OFT Efficient
blogs.description: Demystifies the technical side of OFT for readers with a mild math background. It explains Cayley parameterization, why block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices reduce parameters, and compares the parameter count to LoRA’s low‑rank updates using simple diagrams and analogies.

blogs.title: Future Directions: Compositional Orthogonal Finetuning and Beyond
blogs.description: Looks ahead at the open problems highlighted by the authors – composability of orthogonal transforms, scaling challenges with matrix inverses, and improving parameter efficiency. The post speculates on potential applications such as stacking multiple customizations or extending OFT to other generative architectures.
